problem: Outdoor VLN agents (Touchdown, Map2Seq) remain far from human performance, and prior diagnostics looked at tokens, visual cues or junction types but ignored the high-level shape of routes. Train and test routes share the same few action patterns, so reported generalization may be confounded by pattern leakage.
motivation: Both datasets contain only ~85 (TD) and ~63-66 (M2S) unique patterns of actions over thousands of samples, so test routes largely repeat training shapes. Knowing how much success stems from memorized route shapes rather than grounding is needed for proper dataset design and evaluation.
key_idea: Define Pattern of Actions (PAct), the abstract sequence of turns and forwards describing a route's shape, and show that LLM-based VLN agents depend on PActs seen in training, using pattern-disjoint splits and pattern-filling synthetic data augmentation.
insight: Swapping in instructions from routes with the same PAct still yields success (up to ~6% TC even without vision) while different-PAct instructions give ~1-2%, so the agent partly exploits route shape. Pattern-disjoint splits (0-pact, 0-pact-geo) versus size-matched controls (base-p, base-pg) reduce TC, worsen orientation F1 (up to ~10 points) and mostly raise overshoot rate, and this holds even with no vision. Template-based synthetic data covering missing patterns helps modestly on Map2Seq (~+2.5 points), with the combined noise/new-town settings best (Table 17).
method: Pattern of Actions (PAct): the route's ground-truth action sequence with consecutive forwards collapsed, hashed as a string (e.g. frfrfs); gives 85 unique patterns in TouchDown and 66 in Map2Seq.
Instruction swapping test: replace each test route's instruction with 5 instructions from routes with the same PAct vs 5 from different PAct, and compare TC on base-unseen.

Pattern-disjoint splits: 0-pact (patterns sorted by frequency and alternately assigned to train/test, 50-50 split) and 0-pact-geo-a/b (also geographically separate), each with size-matched controls base-p and base-pg-a/b.
Sub-task analysis: task completion, orientation (multi-class initial action, macro P/R/F1) and overshoot rate (reached but failed to stop).
Agent: VELMA-style modular LLM agent (Llama1/2-7B, Mistral-7B, LoRA fine-tuned 20 epochs) with OpenCLIP landmark grounding or a no-vision variant.

Pattern-filling data augmentation: enumerate all patterns with up to 7 turns (508 TD, 127 M2S), fill instruction templates with landmarks, paraphrase with GPT-4o, and create 10,160 samples, adding noise (word/letter drop, repeated observations), synthetic 'new town' landmarks and zero-initial-turn variants.

setting.backbone: Llama-2-7B (main), Llama-1-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1 (LoRA fine-tuned) + OpenCLIP for landmark grounding
setting.training_data: TouchDown (9,326 routes) and Map2Seq (7,672 routes) human-annotated data with various splits; optionally +10,160 synthetic template/GPT-4o-paraphrased samples
setting.observation: Street-view panoramas, converted by OpenCLIP into textual landmark descriptions (or no vision)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph actions: FORWARD, LEFT, RIGHT, TURN_AROUND, STOP

numbers.extra: VELMA-style fine-tuning, baseline human data only

numbers_note: Paper is an analysis study; main results are TC under custom pattern-disjoint splits (Tables 2,3,10,11) rather than a leaderboard. Only base-unseen and DA numbers listed; 'TC' is task completion. Benchmark names Touchdown/Map2Seq are not in the canonical list; bench field uses them as printed.
results: Removing shared patterns between train and test lowers TC (e.g. Llama2 TD→TD 28.34→24.28 with vision, 15.58→7.77 without; up to ~8.9 points in some settings), lowers orientation F1 and raises overshoot rates. Simple pattern-filling data augmentation improves M2S TC by up to ~2.5 points (36.75→39.25) but slightly hurts TD→TD.
limitations: Only LLM-based modular agents (Llama/Mistral 7B) in discrete outdoor Manhattan environments with English instructions; indoor, continuous and end-to-end models are not studied.
Data augmentation is preliminary, with a fixed hyperparameter setting and small, inconsistent gains (slight drop on TouchDown).
